questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
A government wants to move its economy away from central planning towards a market economy. Which policy would be consistent with this aim?

options.A: introduce tariffs on imported goods
options.B: privatise the ownership of electricity generation
options.C: provide free education for primary school pupils
options.D: reduce prices of foods such as wheat and rice

questions.questionText: What would be a determinant of a country’s production possibility curve boundary?

options.A: the capital invested in infrastructure
options.B: the level of price and wage inflation
options.C: the level of unemployed labour
options.D: the volume of imports and exports

questions.questionText: What justifies government intervention in the provision of a merit good such as education?

options.A: People who pay for education value it more than those who cannot pay.
options.B: Private schools have more merit than state schools.
options.C: Social costs of providing education outweigh social benefits of education.
options.D: Some consumers do not fully recognise the value of education.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the supply of limestone from quarry X and quarry Y at two prices. price of S X limestone S Y P P O Q Q
What is a perfectly contestable market?

options.A: a market in which the costs of entry and exit are zero
options.B: a market in which there are high barriers to entry
options.C: a market that has high sunk costs
options.D: a market that uses price discrimination

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand for and supply of cream. The original equilibrium is point X. Strawberries and cream are complementary goods. If the price of strawberries falls and the cost of producing cream increases which point represents the new equilibrium? S price 2 S of cream 1 S B C

options.A: X D D D
options.D: 1 O quantity of cream

questions.questionText: Hunters in Mozambique want to extract wild honey from beehives. They find the beehives by following birds known as honeyguide birds who want the beeswax that is also found in the beehives. What does this suggest?

options.A: Hunters and honeyguide birds are rival consumers.
options.B: Wild honey and beeswax are free goods.
options.C: Wild honey and beeswax are in joint supply.
options.D: Wild honey is the opportunity cost of beeswax.

questions.questionText: What follows if the income elasticity of demand for a good has a value of –0.2?

options.A: When income rises less of the good is bought.
options.B: When income rises more of the good is bought.
options.C: When price falls more of the good is bought.
options.D: When price rises less of the good is bought.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between price (P) and demand (D) for a normal good G. S price of good G P D D O Q quantity demanded of good G What would cause a shift to D ?

options.A: a decrease in the price of a substitute good
options.B: a fall in the level of advertising for the good G
options.C: a rise in the price of good G
options.D: an increase in the incomes of consumers

questions.questionText: What is most likely to cause an increase in the consumer surplus in the market for a normal good?

options.A: an increase in consumer incomes
options.B: an increase in the number of substitute goods
options.C: an increase in the price of a complementary good
options.D: an increase in the price of the good

questions.questionText: The cross elasticity of demand between two products, X and Y, is negative. What would be the immediate effect of a rise in the price of product Y?

options.A: Quantity demanded of product X will fall.
options.B: Supply of product X will rise.
options.C: The cross elasticity of demand will rise.
options.D: The price of product X will rise.

questions.questionText: Which combination of events is most likely to leave the demand curve for a normal good in the same position?

options.A: a decrease in consumer incomes and an increase in the price of a substitute good
options.B: a decrease in consumer incomes and an increase in the price of the good
options.C: an increase in consumer incomes and an increase in the price of a substitute good
options.D: an increase in consumer incomes and an increase in the price of the good

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a transfer payment?

options.A: the advertising expenditure of a firm
options.B: the allowance given by a parent to their child while at school
options.C: the rent paid to a land owner by a tenant farmer
options.D: the wage paid to a worker in the government service

questions.questionText: Too much sugar causes an increase in a consumer’s weight. A government has introduced a ‘sugar tax’ on the consumption of soft drinks that have a high sugar content. How might this policy help to reduce the number of overweight people?

options.A: Consumers switch to cheaper brands of soft drink with a high sugar content.
options.B: Consumers switch to other high-sugar substitute goods, such as alcohol or sweets.
options.C: The price elasticity of demand for soft drinks is inelastic.
options.D: The tax revenue is spent on education about the dangers of soft drink consumption.

questions.questionText: A government intends to introduce a minimum price for rice, a maximum price for heating oil and a tax on chewing gum. Who, in each market, is meant to benefit from these policies? market for rice market for heating oil market for chewing gum

options.A: consumers government producers
options.B: government producers government
options.C: producers producers consumers
options.D: producers consumers government

questions.questionText: A Southern African government was concerned about the market influence of a large producer and was keen to take control of the company. What might be the possible result of this?

options.A: an increase in the role of the market
options.B: an increase in public ownership
options.C: an increase in the role of the consumer
options.D: an increase in the amount of competition

questions.questionText: What describes a regressive tax?

options.A: All taxpayers pay the same proportion of income in taxes.
options.B: High-income earners pay a lower proportion of income in taxes than low-income earners.
options.C: High-income earners pay less in taxes than low-income earners.
options.D: High-income earners pay more in taxes than low-income earners.

questions.questionText: A country has a fixed exchange rate. Which combination of problems would be most likely to cause the country’s government to reduce taxation and lower interest rates?

options.A: demand inflation and a balance of payments current account deficit
options.B: demand inflation and a low level of investments
options.C: high unemployment and a balance of payments current account deficit
options.D: high unemployment and a low level of investment

questions.questionText: How can a change in consumption that increases unemployment be illustrated on an aggregate demand and aggregate supply diagram? effect on the aggregate demand curve effect on the aggregate supply curve

options.A: movement down the demand curve shift outwards
options.B: movement up the demand curve shift inwards
options.C: shift inwards movement down the supply curve
options.D: shift inwards movement up the supply curve

questions.questionText: What is not an item in a country’s current account of its balance of payments?

options.A: exports of primary commodities
options.B: money received from banking services
options.C: overseas investment
options.D: profits sent back by companies overseas

questions.questionText: A country decides to remove all its tariffs and engage in free international trade. What will be the final decision the country has to make before free trade takes place?

options.A: deciding which resources to allocate to the production of goods and services for international trade
options.B: deciding which goods and services should be provided for international trade
options.C: identifying the opportunity costs of production of goods and services which might be used for international trade
options.D: setting an appropriate exchange rate for the international trade of goods and services

questions.questionText: What is assumed to be constant when drawing an aggregate demand curve?

options.A: government tax revenue
options.B: interest rates
options.C: the level of unemployment
options.D: the money supply

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the imposition of an import tariff. S is world supply. W S + tax is world supply after the tariff is imposed. W S domestic price S + tax W S W D O q q q q
An economy is experiencing a period of deflation. What must be happening?

options.A: The average price level is falling.
options.B: The output of the economy is falling.
options.C: The rate of inflation is falling.
options.D: The real value of money is falling.

questions.questionText: A British citizen buys a house in the US which he rents to American citizens in order to receive an income for himself. Where will the initial purchase and then the rent be recorded on the UK balance of payments? initial purchase rent

options.A: capital account export current account import
options.B: capital account import current account export
options.C: current account export capital account import
options.D: current account import capital account export

questions.questionText: Under a system of floating exchange rates, what determines the foreign exchange value of a currency?

options.A: the overall supply of and demand for a currency on currency markets
options.B: the purchasing power of the currency relative to the purchasing power of foreign currencies
options.C: the surplus or deficit on the balance of payments on current account
options.D: the differential between domestic and foreign interest rates

questions.questionText: A country with a balance of trade deficit raises interest rates. How may this help to reduce the deficit in the short run?

options.A: by increasing the inflow of foreign direct investment
options.B: by lowering the foreign exchange rate
options.C: by raising the level of domestic capital investment
options.D: by reducing the level of domestic aggregate demand

questions.questionText: An economy is currently in the position PY shown on the diagram. SRAS price level P AD O Y real GDP Which short-run effects is government spending on education likely to have on unemployment and inflation? unemployment inflation

options.A: fall fall
options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall
options.D: rise rise
